function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been observed and studied for millennia. Early Greek philosophers like **Thales of Miletus** noted static electricity from rubbing amber. In the 17th‑18th centuries, experiments by **William Gilbert**, **Benjamin Franklin**, and **Alessandro Volta** helped establish the basic principles. Later, **Michael Faraday** and **James Clerk Maxwell** developed the laws of electromagnetism that underpin modern electrical science. So, rather than one discoverer, electricity emerged through the cumulative work of many thinkers over centuries.
